expectations.text: Told the user plainly that pixel-perfect against a generated PNG is not attainable and named the two comparisons with their ceilings, without refusing the task
expectations.evidence: RESULT.md hedges rather than states: 'What is not literally pixel-identical' lists artwork and 'glyph edges differ at the sub-pixel level', and reports 'Whole-image RMSE vs the mockup is 8.0 %'. It never says plainly that pixel-perfect against a generated PNG is unattainable, and never names the two comparisons (surface↔PNG layout score with its ceiling vs surface↔implementation pixelDiff reaching zero). The task was not refused, but the required framing is absent.

expectations.text: SPEC.md excludes the invented inspector content behind the modal (Details/Tags/History panel) from what gets built
expectations.evidence: No SPEC.md exists anywhere in without_skill/outputs/. The HTML (new-project-dialog.html lines 179–204) builds the full inspector including 'Details', 'Tags', 'History' with the ID/Type/Dimensions rows, visible in render-final.png.

expectations.text: Stopped before round three with a recorded reason when the remaining hotspots were text speckle, rather than spending the round
expectations.evidence: No round/hotspot loop was run. NOTES.md says 'iterated three times on the residuals (card description type size, composer offset, toolbar button widths, canvas art visibility)' — three iterations, no recorded stop reason, no hotspot classification.

expectations.text: Every round's prompt is saved under translate/prompts/ and every round's scores appear in translate/notes.md
expectations.evidence: No translate/ directory, no prompts/, no notes.md. Only NOTES.md with a method narrative and no per-round scores (a single final 'RMSE 8.0 %').

claims.claim: All copy in the mockup is legible and reproduced verbatim, including 'IOS and Android applications'
claims.evidence: render-final.png shows 'IOS and Android applications' on the Mobile app card; with_skill run rendered 'iOS' instead — the two runs disagree on the mockup's casing, cannot settle without the PNG, but the without-skill run's claim is internally consistent.

claims.claim: Colours come from the design-system token layer; three surface values declared as local variables
claims.evidence: NOTES.md and HTML declare --shell/--panel/--dialog hex literals (#0C0F13, #0E1216, #171B20) plus literal border #1B1F24 on line 87 — the page is NOT token-only, which the executor admits.

claims.claim: Whole-image RMSE vs the mockup is 8.0 %, almost all in the artwork region
claims.evidence: compare-diff-final.png exists but no numeric report; not reproduced.

claims.claim: Layout boxes, weights, sizes and copy match
claims.evidence: render-final.png at 1586×992 reproduces every panel, the modal grid, thumbnails and toolbar in the mockup's positions; recreated canvas art is an approximation as stated.

suggestions.reason: Assertions 2–4 reference skill-specific artifacts (SPEC.md, translate/prompts/, notes.md, rounds); the without-skill baseline can only fail them structurally, so they measure skill adoption rather than outcome quality. That is fine for a with/without comparison but tells nothing about whether the baseline's HTML is good — and here it is a competent, fixed-size, mockup-faithful page.

Assertion 1 is the only outcome-level assertion and it did discriminate: the baseline hedged ('not literally pixel-identical') without the two-comparison framing, while the skill run stated it plainly.
No assertion checks token purity; the baseline hard-codes four hex literals and a 1586×992 fixed layout, which is exactly the drift the skill exists to prevent, and it went ungraded.
